title: Jimmy Jackson's Royal K Jacksonian Society Syncopators in Hillsdale
summary: Summer 1922 with a doctor's son's band on a riverboat-style hall in Michigan, while Davison moves among banjo, cornet, alto horn and mellophone.

bands.name: Jimmy Jackson's Royal K Jacksonian Society Syncopators

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Who played what: early band size and instrumentation

blocks.x: bands; they had--- we had a clown band in that town which was they dressed up in clown suits but they only played things like fairs and things like that, but there was another guy there that had a band; his name was James Jackson and he was a doctor's son and he played the drums and, uh, he was a damn good drummer and I played one summer with him as well.
That was the summer of 1922 --

1922 - yes - he had a--- his father was very rich and he bought a place that looked like an old riverboat - up in Hillsdale, Michigan on a lake - yeah - and his--- the name of his band was "Jimmy Jackson's Royal K Jacksonian Society Syncopators ". Now, there's a name for you.
That was a hot one.
Yeah - that was a big time name.
He later did go on and played in Chicago --
Yes, he had a big band at one time.
Yes.

Well, anyway, I did a summer with him and now I'm getting more and more on the cornet but I picked up - from a friend who had an alto horn and I found out that I could blow that alto too. So, I was playing banjo, mostly banjo, and some trumpet and a little

mellophone. And, of course, you know the mellophone is in another key; the mellophone is in E flat; the trumpet is B flat and I would have to sit down and work out the fingering from one horn to the other work out and I used play a little jazz courses on the mellophone.
Had you done any guitar yet?
No, no--- yes - four string.
Oh - that was all. Not much.
But, it was an instrument that wasn't very popular and I don't think it ever was very popular.
Well, I think earlier, you said alto horn - unless I misheard you---
Alto horn - yes.
What is that now?
That's an E flat alto horn they use in marching bands.
Is that the mellophone?

Yes - well, they call it mellophone--- Actually, they called them peck-horns. People say he plays the peck-horn-- that's an hmm cha-cha hmm cha-cha, sound if you get in the band, a big marching band. And, so then, I'm trying to think what I did from there---
After you played that summer with Jimmy Jackson - that was in Hillsdale, Michigan--
Yeah - Hillsdale---
